outcome: A July 2026 preprint by Tao Zhang claims both directions of Fuglede's conjecture fail in dimension two (via finite-group counterexamples in Z60xZ12 transferred to unions of unit squares in R^2), but an independent review flags that the non-tiling direction's transference argument, as printed, rests on a notational error that must be fixed before the result can be accepted; no expert digestion, journal acceptance, or corrected version has surfaced. Separately, a July 2026 preprint by Ruxi Shi settles Fuglede's conjecture in R for the class of bounded sets that are unions of three intervals (a genuine case of the one-dimensional part of this bullet), with no error reported. No AI system involvement was found in either paper.

counterexample.object: Two explicit 60-point subsets of the finite Abelian group Z60 x Z12 (one a translational tile that is not spectral, the other spectral but not a tile), transferred via a finite-to-infinite transference principle to bounded subsets of R^2 that are finite unions of unit squares.
counterexample.verified_how: Direct construction in a finite Abelian group, claimed to lift to R^2 by an explicit transference argument; the lifting step for the non-tiling direction is disputed (see disputes).

disputes.summary: A review on pith.science of arXiv:2607.15632 states that the non-tiling direction of Zhang's construction 'rests on a notational error that must be fixed' in the transference proof, and that if patched, the result would resolve the two-dimensional case; as printed, the paper's claim for that direction is not established. No corrected version (v2) has appeared on arXiv as of this research, and no independent expert (e.g. a named mathematician's blog, a journal, or a citing follow-up paper) has publicly verified or endorsed the result.

summary: The Wikipedia bullet asks about nonconvex sets in R and R^2 (the last two open dimensions of Fuglede's conjecture; counterexamples were already known for d>=3 before the frozen revision). Two relevant preprints appeared in the window, both in July 2026. (1) Tao Zhang (arXiv:2607.15632, submitted 2026-07-17, Xidian University) claims both directions of the conjecture fail in dimension two, via an explicit construction in Z60xZ12 lifted to R^2. I read the full paper (via the HTML rendering): the construction is described in detail, the acknowledgements credit only Chinese NSF/Shaanxi grant funding, and there is no mention anywhere of computer search, machine learning, or AI tools in the discovery or verification of the result. However, a review on pith.science (an independent paper-review site) reports that the non-tiling direction's transference argument, as printed, rests on a notational error ('R_k notation error') that must be corrected before the two-dimensional case can be considered resolved. I could not find any later arXiv version (only v1 exists), any citing paper, or any established mathematician's public digestion (Terence Tao's blog has no post on this, and his only Fuglede-tagged post predates the window by 15 years and concerns a different topic, the Coven-Meyerowitz conjecture). Given a live, unretracted but disputed correctness issue and no expert digestion, I classify this as 'claimed' rather than 'resolved' or 'partial'. (2) Ruxi Shi (arXiv:2607.24005, submitted 2026-07-27) proves that every bounded measurable subset of R that is spectral and a union of three intervals must tile R by translation — a genuine case of the R part of the bullet (restricting to three-interval sets), with no reported error and no AI mentioned. This alone would support 'partial' status (a case settled, direction=confirmed) for the R part, but since the dimension-two claim is the larger and more central event and carries an open correctness question, I record the record's overall status as 'claimed' and describe both events here rather than picking one arbitrarily, per the instruction to describe multiple events in summary rather than invent extra records. No AI system was found to be involved in either paper: not in acknowledgements, not in described methodology (both read as traditional analytic/algebraic constructions), and a broad search for AI-mathematics breakthroughs in 2026 (which turned up unrelated results — Jacobian conjecture via 'Fable AI', unit distance problem via an OpenAI internal model, Erdos problems via DeepMind's AlphaEvolve-like system) never surfaced Fuglede's conjecture. The Wikipedia 'List of mathematical discoveries by artificial intelligence' page, checked independently, also does not mention Fuglede's conjecture. A tangential GitHub issue (google-deepmind/formal-conjectures #5703) flags a Lean misformalization of the (unrelated, d>=3) 'fails in every dimension' variant, found via an automated LLM audit — but this is bookkeeping on an already-settled higher-dimensional variant, not a result on the R/R^2 case, and the project's own README states AI (AlphaProof) is used only to catch misformalizations, not to produce proofs, so this is ai_role 'none' territory and not part of this record's core event regardless.
competing_reading: One could argue the Zhang paper should be scored 'partial' with resolution_direction 'refuted' on the grounds that the tiling-direction counterexample (a tile with no spectrum) may be unaffected by the notational error, which the review says affects only the non-tiling (spectral-but-not-tiling) direction — in which case one full direction of the conjecture in dimension two would already be established as false, while the other remains claimed-but-unverified. I did not have enough detail from the review to confirm that the error is isolated to only one direction with certainty, so I did not split the record this way; if the error is confirmed to affect only one direction, the correct status might be 'partial' (one direction refuted) rather than 'claimed' (whole result pending fix). Alternatively, one could argue the correct denominator-relevant status should rest solely on the Shi three-intervals result (clearly a case, clearly correct) and treat the Zhang claim purely as 'progress', since it is unverified; I judged 'claimed' more appropriate because the author explicitly presents a complete resolution of the last open Euclidean dimension, not merely a bound.
what_would_settle_it: A corrected version of arXiv:2607.15632 (v2 or later) fixing the flagged transference-proof error, together with either a citing paper, a named mathematician's public digestion (e.g., a blog post or MathOverflow answer working through the argument), or journal acceptance, would move the dimension-two claim to 'resolved' or clarify if only 'partial'. Absent that, watching for retraction or silent abandonment (no update for a long period after a flagged error) would support reclassifying toward 'open' or 'open_stale'-adjacent treatment of the dimension-two claim specifically.

corrections.why: SCOPE: `claimed` counted this among resolutions, but the bullet asks about both R and R^2, and Zhang's construction concerns dimension two only; R stays open, with Shi's three-interval result a further case there. One of the two dimensions the bullet names is a case, `partial` under 6.1, with `resolution_direction` staying `refuted`. Zhang's claim is not set aside: the only flag against it is an automated reviewer's report of a notational error in one direction, which is not a knock-down. The research rules fold 'how much was settled' and 'has an expert checked it' into one field, and the agent read an unreviewed result as `claimed`; that is the pattern this batch of corrections fixes.

judgement.doubts: The bullet names R and R^2; Zhang addresses only R^2, so even if correct it is a case (the earlier correction's reasoning is right). Both events are partial-tier; Zhang is chosen as the more far-reaching (a whole dimension vs. a class of three-interval sets). Had Shi been chosen the direction would be confirmed; overall the settled cases arguably go both ways. Zhang's non-tiling direction rests on a transference step flagged by an automated reviewer; the tile-not-spectral direction may stand alone. No AI in either paper.
